newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian stocks advance, foreigners seen buying.
newsitem.headline: Latvian stocks advance, foreigners seen buying.

text.p: Latvian stock prices advanced significantly on Wednesday with foreign buyers seen entering the market although turnover slipped, dealers said.
Total market turnover fell to 91,000 lats but the Rietumu Bank market index grew 4.62 percent to a new record of 157.72, or 1.95 percent above its January peak.
"Prices of all the big stocks have been advancing. Most probably large foreign investors are involved," broker Zigmunds Pavlovskis of the Baltijas Tranzitu bank said.
Market leader Unibanka roared ahead, registering its second record high in two days. It hit 3.45 lats, a jump of 15 santimes.
Unibanka also saw the bourse's second biggest turnover of 17,700 lats.

Daugavpils Chain factory, a secondary list share currently preparing to move to the official list, led the market with turnover of 20,300 lats as it put on almost 15 percent or 34 santimes to 2.67 lats.
Lode Brick factory edged up a notch to 2.06 lats against 2.05 on turnover of 13.400 lats.
Elsewhere on the official list, Riga Transport Fleet traded 10,600 lats and fell three santimes to 1.65 lats.
Other official list share, Staburadze confectionery, also closed lower at 2.58 against 2.60 on trade of 3,500 lats.
Mangali Shipyard also gained ground adding two santimes to 1.12 lats on volume of 1,800 lats.
Ventspils fish cannery rose another 20 santimes or some 14 percent to 1.58 lats as shares worth 1,100 lats changed hands.
